title: Quick check: Handling Form Submission

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Handling Form Submission”?
options: The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Submit handlers should handle non-OK responses and represent loading, success, empty, and failure states.
questions.answer_key: Submit handlers should handle non-OK responses and represent loading, success, empty, and failure states.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Handling Form Submission: Submit handlers should handle non-OK responses and represent loading, success, empty, and failure states.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Submit handlers?
options: Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
Check response.ok before parsing success data and handle cancellation or out-of-order responses.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
questions.answer_key: Check response.ok before parsing success data and handle cancellation or out-of-order responses.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Handling Form Submission: Check response.ok before parsing success data and handle cancellation or out-of-order responses.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Handling Form Submission” complete?
options: Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Handling Form Submission: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
